function: Multi-source DOA estimation from raw uplink data snapshots of sparse arrays (attention-only transformer); DOAs then prune or set downlink beams in MU-MIMO beam management (pp. 6–8, 13).
system: BS with 5-element sparse array (MRA, aperture 10; also 15 elements), 3–20 sources, 15 GHz; beam stage: 64-antenna ULA, 10 users; no RIS (pp. 9, 13).
method: Attention-only transformer (Snap-TF), 2–3 single-head layers, d_attn = 96, mean pooling; supervised on sorted DOA labels, SGD, 100 epochs, SNR −20 to 20 dB (pp. 7–10).
data_channel: Own synthetic narrowband array model, random path losses, Gaussian/16QAM/QPSK symbols; per K, 2×10⁶ training, 6×10⁴ validation, 1×10⁴ test samples; no standard channel or measurements (pp. 4, 9–10).
test_conditions: Trained at T = 50 snapshots, SNR −20 to 20 dB; tested without retraining at T = 10–100 and on mixed QPSK+16QAM symbols (Fig. 6, pp. 10–11).
baselines: Learned: DCR-T, DCR-G-Fro, DCR-G-Aff, SRL-GD (CNN covariance reconstruction plus Root-MUSIC); non-learned: Oracle Root-MUSIC on a 10-element ULA (bound), full codebook sweeping (pp. 9–14).
metrics: DOA MSE (rad²) versus SNR, snapshots, sources; runtime and trainable parameters; system throughput (bps/Hz) versus coherence time and reciprocity mismatch; beam sweeping overhead (pp. 10–15).
complexity: Order O(⌈log2(k+1)⌉T²d_attn) (p. 9); 0.356M parameters versus about 11M, runtime about 1.1 ms versus 2.2× (small) to 31.3× (large) slower benchmarks (pp. 11–12, Fig. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "K narrowband and far-field sources" impinge on the array (eq. 1, p. 4), and p. 9: "the path losses are generated as i.i.d. preliminary samples"; the data come from the authors' own synthetic array model, and no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "directly tested in different cases without retraining or tuning" (T = 10–100 versus T = 50 in training); p. 11: "different, or even mixed, modulation types that it was not trained on".
q3_support: p. 5: "which will serve as important benchmarks later" (the earlier learned DOA methods DCR-T, DCR-G-Fro, DCR-G-Aff, and SRL-GD, compared on DOA MSE in Figs. 5–7); non-learned references are p. 12: "applying Root-MUSIC to the sample SCM of a physical 10-element ULA" (an ideal Oracle bound, Fig. 9) and p. 13: "Codebook only (full sweeping)" in the beam stage.
q4_support: p. 12: "that of the proposed Snap-TF algorithm (with 3 layers) is around 0.356 million in both setups", versus about 11 and 17 million for the benchmarks; p. 11: "consistently achieves sub-millisecond level runtime under both system configurations, approximately 1.103 ms"; the order is given on p. 9.
q5_support: p. 15: "We also thank Dr. Kuan-Lin Chen from UCSD for sharing the codes of [34]" refers to the code of a benchmark; the paper gives no link to its own code or data, and its data are synthetic (pp. 9–10).
notes: Borderline function: the learned model is a DOA estimator, which is excluded when alone, but Section VI (pp. 13–14) feeds its DOAs into downlink beam management, pruning candidates or setting beams directly, with non-learned sweeping, LS, and ZF; the abstract presents this as a second contribution, so it is included as ISAC (area 5). The reviewer may exclude with reason function if the beam stage is not read as the learned method's function. The PDF is arXiv:2506.23525v2, the manuscript accepted by JSAC on 5 Jan 2026 (p. 1), and prints no DOI. Borderline q3: the non-learned comparisons are an ideal Oracle bound (Fig. 9) and full codebook sweeping (Fig. 13); no practical non-learned DOA estimator is compared.
